newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Japanese consortium wins Uzbek airport tender.
newsitem.headline: Japanese consortium wins Uzbek airport tender.

text.p: A consortium of Japan's Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui and Company Ltd and Shemizu have won a tender to modernise three airports in Uzbekistan, a local official said on Tuesday.

Project coordinator Abdulla Khairullayev told Reuters that the three companies would be given about half of an investment 17.28 billion yen earmarked for the overhaul of airports in Samarkand, Bukhara and Urgench.
The companies will improve runways, landing equipment and lighting at airports and aim to complete work by September.
Another tender will be held later this year to select a company or companies to modernise passenger facilities and air traffic control systems at the airports.
Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund, or OECF, has said it will extend a 15.20 billion yen credit to the Uzbek government for the programme.
Other funds totalling about 1.72 billion yen, will come from Uzbekistan's Khavo Yullari national airline.
Khairullayev said the OECF loan to the government was at 2.7 percent annual with a grace period of 10 years.
